The Art of the Onam Sadya: 26 Dishes on a Banana Leaf
Our head chef walks you through the order, the flavours and the etiquette of Kerala's grand feast

Every Onam our kitchen starts at 4 a.m. to prepare a full Sadya: avial, olan, kaalan, thoran, sambar, rasam, three kinds of payasam and much more, served in a precise order on a fresh banana leaf.

The secret is balance. Sweet, sour, salty, bitter, pungent and astringent flavours all appear on the leaf so that every bite feels new. Start with parippu and ghee, finish with payasam and a banana.

Want to learn it yourself? Join our Kerala Sadya Cooking Masterclass, seats are limited.
From Bean to Cup: How We Brew Our Filter Coffee
Single-origin Chikmagalur beans, a slow brass filter and a little chicory

Our café sources Arabica and Robusta beans from two family estates in Chikmagalur and roasts them in small batches every Monday.

The decoction drips slowly through a traditional brass filter for 15 minutes before we blend it with frothy hot milk, poured from a height to get that perfect foam.

Try it with our crisp ghee roast dosa, the combination our regulars swear by.
Soft Appam & Chicken Stew: A Family Recipe
The Sunday breakfast that made our restaurant famous, now in your kitchen

Soak 2 cups of raw rice for 5 hours, grind with grated coconut and cooked rice, add yeast and sugar and let the batter ferment overnight.

For the stew, simmer chicken with ginger, green chillies, whole spices and potatoes in thin coconut milk, then finish with thick coconut milk and a few curry leaves.

Swirl the batter in a hot appachatti so the edges turn lacy and the centre stays soft.
5 Healthy Lunch Bowls Under 500 Calories
Millet, sprouts and grilled fish: new on our corporate lunch menu

Our office customers asked for lighter lunches, so the kitchen built five bowls around millets, sprouts, grilled fish and seasonal vegetables.

Every bowl is under 500 calories and packed in compostable boxes for our corporate lunch subscriptions.
Latte Art for Beginners: The Heart, Tulip and Rosetta
Our baristas share the three pours every café lover should learn

Great latte art starts with silky micro-foam: steam whole milk to 60°C and keep the wand just below the surface.

Pour from high to mix, then bring the jug close and wiggle for a rosetta. Join our next Latte Art Workshop to practise with our baristas.
